heading.en: Slice a cone, get a curve

hook.en: A torch beam on a wall, the path of a thrown ball, a planet going round the Sun: all these curves come from cutting a double cone with a plane.
hook.kn: ಗೋಡೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಟಾರ್ಚ್ ಬೆಳಕು, ಎಸೆದ ಚೆಂಡಿನ ದಾರಿ, ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಸುತ್ತ ಸುತ್ತುವ ಗ್ರಹ: ಈ ಎಲ್ಲ ವಕ್ರಗಳು ದ್ವಿಶಂಕುವನ್ನು ಸಮತಲದಿಂದ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿದಾಗ ಸಿಗುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Decide which conic a plane section gives

say.en: A torch beam on a wall, the path of a thrown ball, a planet going round the Sun: all these curves come from cutting a double cone with a plane. In this lesson: Describe the double-napped cone.
Decide which conic a plane section gives.

body.en: Take a fixed vertical line $l$ (the axis) and another line $m$ (the generator) meeting it at V at an angle $\alpha$. Rotating $m$ about $l$ keeping $\alpha$ fixed sweeps out a *double-napped* right circular cone with vertex V; the two parts on either side of V are its nappes. We cut it with a plane making an angle $\beta$ with the axis.
body.kn: ಒಂದು ಓರೆ ರೇಖೆಯನ್ನು ಲಂಬ ಅಕ್ಷದ ಸುತ್ತ ತಿರುಗಿಸಿದರೆ ಶೃಂಗದ ಎರಡೂ ಬದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಶಂಕು ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ದ್ವಿಶಂಕುವನ್ನು ಅಕ್ಷದೊಂದಿಗೆ β ಕೋನ ಮಾಡುವ ಸಮತಲದಿಂದ ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

points.en: α: semi-vertical angle of the cone
β: angle between the cutting plane and the axis

narration.en: Spin a slanted line round a vertical axis and you get a cone on both sides of the vertex. We then cut this double cone with a plane at an angle beta to the axis.

say.en: beta: angle between the cutting plane and the axis.

narration.en: Turn a line about a fixed axis through V, keeping the angle alpha: it sweeps out a double-napped cone. Alpha is the semi-vertical angle.

say.en: Turn a line about a fixed axis through V, keeping the angle alpha: it sweeps out a double-napped cone. Alpha is the semi-vertical angle.
Cut with a plane at right angles to the axis, beta equal to 90 degrees, and the section is a circle.
Tilt the plane a little, so beta is between alpha and 90 degrees. It still cuts right across one nappe: an ellipse.
Tilt it until it is parallel to a generator, beta equal to alpha. The curve never closes: a parabola.
Make the plane steeper still, beta less than alpha, and it cuts both nappes: the two branches of a hyperbola.
Turn a line about a fixed axis through V, keeping the angle alpha: it sweeps out a double-napped cone. Alpha is the semi-vertical angle.

narration.en: Side view of a double cone with semi-vertical angle α (blue) and a cutting plane (yellow) at angle β to the axis. Compare β with α to name the section; a plane through the vertex V gives a degenerate case.
narration.kn: ಅರೆ-ಶೃಂಗ ಕೋನ α ಇರುವ ದ್ವಿ ಶಂಕು (ನೀಲಿ) ಮತ್ತು ಅಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ β ಕೋನದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕತ್ತರಿಸುವ ಸಮತಲ (ಹಳದಿ) ಪಕ್ಕದ ನೋಟ. ಛೇದವನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸಲು β ಅನ್ನು α ಜೊತೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ; V ಮೂಲಕ ಸಮತಲ ಅಪಭ್ರಷ್ಟ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ.

body.en: If the plane does not pass through the vertex: $\beta = 90^\circ$ gives a circle; $\alpha < \beta < 90^\circ$ an ellipse; $\beta = \alpha$ a parabola; $0 \le \beta < \alpha$ a hyperbola (both nappes are cut). If the plane passes through the vertex we get degenerate conics: a point ($\beta > \alpha$), a straight line ($\beta = \alpha$), or a pair of intersecting lines ($0 \le \beta < \alpha$).
body.kn: β ಅನ್ನು α ಜೊತೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ: β = 90° ವೃತ್ತ, α < β < 90° ದೀರ್ಘವೃತ್ತ, β = α ಪರವಲಯ, β < α ಅತಿಪರವಲಯ. ಸಮತಲ ಶೃಂಗದ ಮೂಲಕ ಹೋದರೆ ಬಿಂದು, ರೇಖೆ ಅಥವಾ ಛೇದಿಸುವ ಎರಡು ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಸಿಗುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: Compare beta with alpha. Ninety degrees gives a circle, between alpha and ninety an ellipse, equal to alpha a parabola, and less than alpha a hyperbola.

say.en: alpha < beta is less than 90 degrees: ellipse.
beta equals alpha: parabola.
0 is less than or equal to beta < alpha: hyperbola.

title.en: Which conic does the cut give?

caption.en: For a cone of semi-vertical angle α cut by a plane at angle β to the axis, the eccentricity of the section is e = cos β / cos α. e = 0 is a circle, e < 1 an ellipse, e = 1 a parabola and e > 1 a hyperbola.

narration.en: For a cone of semi-vertical angle α cut by a plane at angle β to the axis, the eccentricity of the section is e = cos β / cos α. e = 0 is a circle, e < 1 an ellipse, e = 1 a parabola and e > 1 a hyperbola. Set β = 90°: e = 0, a circle.

label.en: angle β of the plane with the axis
eccentricity e = cos β / cos α

tryThis.en: Make β equal to α: e becomes exactly 1, a parabola.
Make β smaller than α: e > 1 and the plane cuts both nappes.

say.en: For a cone of semi-vertical angle alpha cut by a plane at angle beta to the axis, the eccentricity of the section is e equals cos beta divided by cos alpha. e equals 0 is a circle, e is less than 1 an ellipse, e equals 1 a parabola and e is greater than 1 a hyperbola. Set beta equals 90 degrees: e equals 0, a circle.

problem.en: A cone has semi-vertical angle α = 30°. A plane not through the vertex makes angle β with the axis. Name the section for β = 90°, 60°, 30° and 20°.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A cone has semi-vertical angle α = 30°. A plane not through the vertex makes angle β with the axis. Name the section for β = 90°, 60°, 30° and 20°.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A cone has semi-vertical angle alpha equals 30 degrees. A plane not through the vertex makes angle beta with the axis. Name the section for beta equals 90 degrees, 60 degrees, 30 degrees and 20 degrees.
beta equals 90 degrees: circle.
beta equals 60 degrees lies between 30 degrees and 90 degrees: ellipse.
beta equals 30 degrees equals alpha: parabola.
beta equals 20 degrees < alpha: hyperbola.
So the answer is Circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola.
